prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1271; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound on the main roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle entered a controlled intersection and was struck on the driver side by Driver 2, whose vehicle was southbound and proceeding through on a green signal. The impact pattern on both vehicles is consistent with a broadside collision at moderate speed. Damage to the driver side of Driver 1's vehicle is largely consistent with the described impact, and photographs taken at the scene confirm several of the reported points of contact. No independent witnesses were located, and no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to responding officers. Driver 1 was seen seated behind the wheel on arrival, and a Passenger was also present in the vehicle, a fact confirmed by both the responding officers and statements from the drivers. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness at the scene, which is consistent with the force and direction of the collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy associated with the vehicle. Medical assistance was requested and the scene was cleared at the end of the investigation.
